evals.name: ts-ship-notify
evals.prompt: When an order is marked as shipped, email the customer that it's on its way. Use the existing mailer. We'll probably add SMS and push notifications later.
evals.expected_output: A small change to markShipped (or its caller) that sends the email through the existing sendEmail function, with the effect visible in the signature or call site and a stated decision about email failure. No notification abstraction for channels that don't exist yet.
expectations: Sends the email by calling sendEmail directly or through a function-typed parameter; no new class, interface, or type named *Service, *Notifier, *Channel, *Manager, or *Factory
Introduces no event bus, observer, queue, channel registry, or plugin mechanism for the future SMS/push channels
Does not send the email when the order was already shipped (the existing early return still short-circuits)

The final message or code states what happens to the order state when sendEmail rejects after updateStatus succeeded (e.g. 'order stays shipped, error propagates, no retry'); a bare await without that statement fails
Adds no new dependency and changes no files besides orders.ts, its caller, and tests

evals.name: go-receipt-test
evals.prompt: Add a unit test for SendReceipt that doesn't hit the network, including the case where sending fails. We'll want to test code that uses the other provider calls later too.
evals.expected_output: SendReceipt accepts a narrow consumer-side interface (one Send method) or a send function instead of *provider.Client, and a test uses a small fake to cover success and failure.
expectations: Declares the interface in package receipts (the consumer), not in package provider
The interface has only the Send method; it does not mirror ListBounces, DeleteDomain, or Stats despite the hint about later tests
The production *provider.Client still satisfies the new parameter type without changes to package provider
The failure test checks the error with errors.Is or errors.As against a sentinel or typed error returned by the fake; comparing only err.Error() or strings fails
Adds no mocking framework or other new module dependency

evals.name: py-discounts
evals.prompt: Support discount codes in pricing: a code is either a percentage off or a fixed amount off the subtotal. Unknown or expired codes must be rejected, and the total can't go below zero. Marketing will likely ask for more discount types later.
evals.expected_output: Two discount kinds modeled as plain data handled by one function, with a narrow exception for invalid codes, codes validated once at the boundary before total() applies them, and Decimal arithmetic with stated rounding.
expectations: Models the two kinds as a union of dataclasses, or a record tagged by an Enum or Literal[...] with exactly one value field, handled with match/if; a record with two optional amount fields fails, as does an abstract base class, Strategy hierarchy, or registry of discount classes
Rejects unknown or expired codes by raising a narrow, named exception (a subclass of ValueError is fine; bare ValueError, returning None, or returning zero fails)

Codes are validated once where they enter (a lookup or parse step that checks unknown and expiry); total() receives only that validated discount value, or validates the code itself. Applying a raw code string without any check fails
Keeps money in Decimal, clamps the total at zero, and quantizes percentage results to cents or states the rounding choice
Keeps the new code in pricing.py (no new utils or discounts package) and adds no new dependency

evals.name: rust-cancel
evals.prompt: Add a Cancelled state with an optional reason, and a cancel function that refuses to cancel jobs that have already finished. More states will follow.
evals.expected_output: A new Job::Cancelled { reason: Option<String> } variant, every match updated explicitly, and cancel taking the reason and returning a Result with a dedicated error type, without consuming the job on refusal.
expectations: Adds a Cancelled variant to the existing enum rather than introducing a State trait or trait objects
Updates label and is_finished by listing the new variant explicitly; no `_` wildcard arm is added
cancel accepts the optional reason and returns Result with a dedicated error type (enum or struct); &str/String errors, panic!, unwrap, or expect fail
cancel does not consume the job on refusal (takes &Job or &mut Job, or returns the job inside the error)
Treats Cancelled as finished in is_finished, or states the choice, and adds no new crate dependency

evals.name: ts-class-convention
evals.prompt: Add a way to void an invoice. Paid invoices can't be voided. We'll be adding more status transition rules soon.
evals.expected_output: A void method on the existing InvoicesService that follows the repo's class-and-DI convention and its existing error classes, with the single rule written directly.
expectations: Adds a method to the existing InvoicesService using the injected repository; does not convert the service to free functions or remove the decorators and constructor injection
Uses the existing NotFoundError for a missing invoice and ConflictError (or another existing error class) for a paid invoice, rather than inventing a result-union convention
Does not refactor or rename unrelated code (send, the repository, the Invoice type)
Writes the paid-invoice rule directly; adds no transition table, state machine, policy object, or rule registry for the future rules
